title: Italian Game
task: White to move: play the typical plan of the Italian Game.
explain: 4.c3 prepares d2–d4 and builds a strong pawn center (Giuoco Piano). 4.O-O or 4.d3 are also good, calm continuations.

title: Ruy López (Spanish Game)
task: White to move: which bishop move turns this into the Spanish Game?
explain: 3.Bb5 attacks the knight on c6 – the defender of e5. That’s the Spanish Game (Ruy López).

title: Sicilian Defense
task: White to move: open the game like in the Open Sicilian.
explain: 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 – White opens the center and gets quick development (Open Sicilian).

title: Queen’s Gambit
task: White to move: offer the Queen’s Gambit.
explain: 2.c4 attacks the central pawn on d5. If Black takes, White usually wins the pawn back and controls the center.

title: London System
task: White to move: which bishop move is the trademark of the London System?
explain: 3.Bf4 – the bishop comes out before e3. Then follow e3, c3, Bd3 and Nbd2: a solid, easy-to-learn system.

title: French Defense
task: White to move: build the classic pawn center against the French.
explain: 2.d4 – White puts two pawns in the center. Black strikes back with 2…d5.

title: Caro-Kann Defense
task: White to move: take the center against the Caro-Kann.
explain: 2.d4 d5 – Black prepares …d5 with c6 without locking in the c8 bishop. White secures the center first.

title: English Opening
task: White to move: open the English way!
explain: 1.c4 – the English Opening controls d5 from the flank. White often follows with g3, Bg2 and Nc3 (fianchetto).

title: Knight fork
task: White to move and win the queen.
explain: 1.Nc7+! attacks king and queen at the same time (fork). After the king moves, 2.Nxa8 follows.

title: Pin
task: White to move and win the queen.
explain: 1.Rae1! pins the queen to its king: it can’t leave the e-file and is lost for a rook.

title: Skewer
task: White to move and win the queen.
explain: 1.Ra6+! – check along the 6th rank. The king has to move, and the queen behind it falls: 2.Rxh6 (skewer).

title: Discovered attack
task: White to move and win material.
explain: 1.Ng5+! – the knight gives check and at the same time opens the e-file: the rook on e1 attacks the queen (discovered attack).

title: Back-rank mate
task: White to move and mate.
explain: 1.Rd8# – Black’s own pawns on f7, g7, h7 lock the king in. A typical back-rank mate.

title: Smothered mate
task: White to move and mate.
explain: 1.Nf7# – the king is surrounded by its own pieces (“smothered”). Only a knight can deliver a mate like this.

title: Double check
task: White to move and mate.
explain: 1.Nd6# – double check by the knight and the rook on e1 (1.Nf6# works the same way). Against double check only a king move helps – and the king has no free square.

title: Queen–bishop battery
task: White to move and mate.
explain: 1.Qxh7# – the bishop on d3 covers h7, the rook on f8 blocks the escape. A classic mate on h7.

title: Pawn fork
task: White to move and win a piece.
explain: 1.d5! attacks the knight on c6 and the bishop on e6 at the same time (pawn fork). One piece is lost.

title: King + queen vs king
task: White to move and mate – but beware of stalemate!
explain: E.g. 1.Qg7# or 1.Qg8# (both protected by the king on f7) or 1.Qh5#/1.Qh6#. Careful: 1.Qg6?? would be stalemate – Black would have no move without being in check!

title: King + rook vs king
task: White to move and mate.
explain: 1.Rh8# – the white king stands in opposition and covers d7, e7, f7; the rook controls the whole 8th rank.

title: Two rooks: ladder mate
task: White to move and mate.
explain: 1.Rb8# – the rook on a7 seals the 7th rank, the second rook mates on the 8th rank. That’s how you “ladder” the king to the edge with two rooks.

title: Opposition
task: White to move and win – king in front of the pawn!
explain: 1.Ke4! (also 1.Kd4 or 1.Kf4) – the king goes IN FRONT of its pawn. Thanks to the spare move e2–e3, White later gains the opposition and pushes the black king aside. A passive move like 1.Kf3? only draws.

title: Lucena position (building a bridge)
task: White to move and win – build the bridge!
explain: 1.Rd1+ Ke7 2.Rd4! Ra1 3.Kc7 Rc1+ 4.Kb6 Rb1+ 5.Kc6 Rc1+ 6.Kb5 Rb1+ 7.Rb4 – the rook builds the “bridge” against the checks.

title: Philidor position
task: Black to move and hold the draw.
explain: 1…Rb6! – the rook holds the 6th rank and keeps the white king from advancing. If the pawn moves to e6, the rook checks from behind (…Rb1).

title: Rule of the square
task: White to move and win: can the black king reach the square?
explain: 1.a5! – the king on f5 can no longer reach the pawn’s square (a5–d5–d8–a8): 1…Ke6 2.a6 Kd7 3.a7 Kc7 4.a8=Q. If White moves the king instead (1.Kg2?), Black steps into the square with 1…Ke5 and catches the pawn.

title: Pawn breakthrough
task: White to move and win.
explain: 1.b6! cxb6 (1…axb6 2.c6! bxc6 3.a6) 2.a6! bxa6 3.c6 – one of the pawns runs through to promote.
